source_row.rationale: Arterial blood gas sampling reflects oxygenated, post-pulmonary blood, providing an accurate assessment of oxygenation status (PaO2) in addition to acid-base status, whereas venous blood gas primarily reflects tissue metabolism and has more limited direct use for assessing oxygenation, though it can still provide useful acid-base and some metabolic information in certain clinical contexts.
source_row.source_detail: PaO2/oxygenation requires arterial sampling; updated 2026 StatPearls, accessed 2026-08-14.
